title: The Elm Street Yard Sale
story: Over Labor Day weekend, four neighbors on Elm Street hauled a hundred odds and ends onto one long table and shared a single cash box. By the time Gus's knee called the rain, each of them had sold exactly one treasure, and the notes in the cash box had turned into soggy scribbles. Before anyone splits the money, who sold what, and for how much?

texts: Dot made more money than Gus.
Vera made more money than the seller of the teapot.
Of the seller who made $4 and the seller who made $8, one is Vera and the other is Linus.
Of the seller of the teapot and the seller of the records, one made $8 and the other made $2.
The seller of the lamp is neither Linus nor Dot.

trace.text: Clue 1 means Dot cannot be $2 and Gus cannot be $8.
Clue 2 means Vera cannot be $2 and the teapot cannot be $8.
Clue 3 limits the choices (mark the X's it gives).
Dot must go with $6: clue 1 rules out $2; clue 3 rules out $4 and $8.
Gus must go with $2: clue 3 rules out $4; clue 1 rules out $8; $6 already goes with Dot.
Clue 4 limits the choices (mark the X's it gives).
The lamp must go with $4: clue 4 rules out $2 and $8; $6 is already ruled out for Dot.
The teapot must go with $2: clue 4 rules out $4 and $6; clue 2 rules out $8.
The birdcage must go with $6: clue 4 rules out $2 and $8; $4 already goes with the lamp.
The records must go with $8: clue 4 rules out $4 and $6; $2 already goes with the teapot.
Dot goes with $6, so Dot also goes with the birdcage.
The lamp must go with Vera: clue 5 rules out Linus and Dot; Gus is already ruled out for $2.
Gus goes with $2, so Gus also goes with the teapot.
Linus must go with the records: clue 5 rules out the lamp; the other choices are already taken.
Linus must go with $8: clue 3 rules out $2 and $6; $4 is already ruled out for the lamp.
Vera must go with $4: clue 2 rules out $2; clue 3 rules out $6; $8 already goes with Linus.
